title: "Class 12. Tell: message, title, annotation, export (solutions)"
format: html
---

**Rule 5, Tell:** the title states the finding. An annotation points to the evidence.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, ggrepel, here)
```

## 1. The one-sentence message (10 minutes, in pairs)

Write one sentence that states what the chart shows. Use numbers. Your partner reads the chart and says the message in their words. Compare the two sentences.

| Topic title | Active title |
|---|---|
| Life expectancy and income in 2007 | In 2007, countries above $10,000 per person lived 15 years longer, on average, than the others |

A title that is too long runs off the plot. Break it with `\n`.

Check the numbers before you write them:

```{r}
#| label: check-message
here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  mutate(group = case_when(income > 10000 ~ "Above $10,000", .default = "Below $10,000")) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarize(countries = n(), mean_life_exp = mean(life_exp))
```

Answer: 54 countries above $10,000 have a mean of 76 years. 88 countries below have a mean of 61 years. The difference is 15 years.

## 2. Title, subtitle, source and annotation

`labs()` sets the text. `\n` starts a new line. `annotate()` adds a note at x and y positions of the data.

```{r}
#| label: tell
here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 10000, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  annotate("text", x = 10500, y = 45, label = "$10,000 per person",
           hjust = 0, color = "gray30") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 12, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  labs(
    title = "In 2007, countries above $10,000 per person\nlived 15 years longer, on average",
    subtitle = "Life expectancy at birth by income per person (log scale).\nCircle area shows population.",
    x = "Income per person (international dollars)",
    y = "Life expectancy (years)",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Gapminder"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title.position = "plot")
```

## 3. Your theme in 3 lines

Copy these three lines to the end of every chart in your capstone. All your graphs then share one look.

```r
theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 4. Export with ggsave()

`ggsave()` saves the last plot you drew. Set the size and the resolution.

```{r}
#| label: export
#| eval: false
ggsave(here("rosling_2007.png"), width = 8, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

Open the PNG. Check that the title fits and that no text overlaps.

## 5. Optional: animate the years

`transition_time(year)` adds one frame per year. Printing the plot renders the animation. This step needs `gganimate` and `gifski`; if the install fails, skip it.

```{r}
#| label: animate
#| eval: false
pacman::p_load(gganimate, gifski)

here("data", "rosling_tidy.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = income, y = life_exp, size = population, color = continent)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 12, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  labs(title = "Year: {round(frame_time)}",
       x = "Income per person (international dollars)",
       y = "Life expectancy (years)", color = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom") +
  transition_time(year)
```

> Deliverable: the exported PNG with an active title, an annotation and your three-line theme.
